nodes.label: Foreman Architect Doctrine
nodes.rationale: Architect runs the highest-judgment model (Fable preferred) and minimizes its own token volume; typing is delegated cross-vendor, and lane reports are never accepted without reading the diff and re-running verification.

nodes.label: Five-Part Spec
nodes.rationale: Subagents share no chat context, so the five-part spec (objective, files, interfaces, constraints, verification) makes context-free delegation to implementer lanes safe.

nodes.label: Cross-Vendor Audit Invariant
nodes.rationale: Never same-vendor audit: decorrelated review from a different model family catches blind spots that same-family self-review misses; if Codex implemented, codex-auditor must not audit.

nodes.label: Reference Environment Inventory
nodes.rationale: Before multi-step implementation the architect runs tool-check scripts, bootstraps missing tools, and only implements after an ENV INVENTORY summary is READY.

nodes.label: Soft Mode
nodes.rationale: High-judgment architect + Grok implementer + Codex GPT-5.6 Sol auditor + Claude advisor at commitment boundaries; ready today needing only Claude Code plus grok and codex CLIs.

nodes.label: Hard Mode
nodes.rationale: Adds worktrees, host-side evidence, independent checks, cold-diff audit, and a deterministic merge gate (INIT->PLAN->IMPLEMENT->CHECK->AUDIT->GATE->PR); Docker worker path still partial.

nodes.label: Codex Auditor (GPT-5.6 Sol)
nodes.rationale: Default read-only audit lane: cold-diff review with no worker chat history, treating the diff as untrusted data; auditor output is advice to the architect/gate, never a ship decision.

nodes.label: Verdict Schema (verdict.schema.json)
nodes.rationale: Schema-forced auditor JSON (APPROVED/WARNING/BLOCKED) beats free-form prose; follows the OpenAI cookbook read-only sandbox + --output-schema code-review pattern.

nodes.label: Codex Implementer
nodes.rationale: Cross-vendor implementation lane used when correctness is critical or to race a second independent implementation against Grok.

nodes.label: Foreman Advisor
nodes.rationale: Second-opinion read-only skeptic consulted sparingly at commitment boundaries (architecture, migrations, API shapes, twice-failed debugging); returns a decisive verdict under ~300 words and never implements.

nodes.label: FOREMAN_REPORT Worktree Report
nodes.rationale: Durable per-worktree report pair (FOREMAN_REPORT.md + .json, schema foreman.worktree-report.v1) written to each tree root so wt-consolidate can gather parallel search/plan/audit results without agents blocking each other.

nodes.label: Grok Implementer
nodes.rationale: Default implementation lane: Grok 4.5 via headless Grok CLI types the code for routine well-specified work; the architect stays on the host model family so typing is cross-vendor.

nodes.label: Grok Evidence Contract
nodes.rationale: Worker claims are not evidence: HEAD SHA and git-status digests recorded before and after invocation detect unauthorized git activity.

nodes.label: Git Discipline (Architect Owns Git Writes)
nodes.rationale: Implementer lanes and their CLIs never run git write commands; the architect owns all git writes so unverified changes cannot be committed by workers.

nodes.label: Foreman QA + Feature Pass (2026-07-15)
nodes.rationale: Frontier-docs research pass validating claimed vs shipped features: soft mode strong, hard mode partial, docs/site drift fixed, live CLI flags for grok and codex validated on-machine, remaining P1/P2 gaps listed.

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Skills load in three stages (discovery, activation, execution) so full instructions load only when a task calls for them, letting agents keep many skills on hand with a small context footprint.

nodes.label: Anthropic Advisor Tool (API)
nodes.rationale: Server-side tool pairing a faster executor model with a higher-intelligence advisor mid-generation: near advisor-solo quality while bulk token generation happens at executor rates.

nodes.label: Claude Code Agent Teams
nodes.rationale: Experimental multi-session coordination: a lead plus independent teammates with shared task list and mailboxes; best for parallel research, competing hypotheses, and cross-layer work, at higher token cost than subagents.

nodes.label: Adversarial Review Step
nodes.rationale: A reviewer in a fresh context sees only the diff and the criteria, not the reasoning that produced the change, so it evaluates the result on its own terms before work is counted done.

nodes.label: Managed Agents Multiagent Orchestration
nodes.rationale: Coordinator agent delegates to a pinned roster of agents in isolated session threads sharing one sandbox; patterns that work: parallelization, specialization, escalation.

nodes.label: Claude Code Custom Subagents
nodes.rationale: Markdown + YAML frontmatter definitions with per-agent model, tool allowlists, permission modes, isolation: worktree, and preloaded skills; each subagent runs in a fresh isolated context and returns only a summary.

nodes.label: Architect Pattern (Tokens Route by Volume)
nodes.rationale: The most expensive model emits the fewest tokens (judgment and specs) while cheap lanes emit the most (code); implementation mechanics are ~90% of session tokens and Grok 4.5 handles them at near-parity, so routing runs far cheaper than Fable-for-everything with cross-vendor review built into the routing rather than bolted on.

nodes.label: wt-merge.sh squash-apply script
nodes.rationale: Squash-applies a worktree branch as staged changes without committing by default, and fails closed (exit codes 3/4/5/7 for missing metadata, dirty index, overlap, conflict) so nothing partial ever lands; overlap refusal makes shared-checkout collisions mechanical to catch.

nodes.label: docs-check.sh documentation & comment-quality gate
nodes.rationale: Documentation quality is enforced by fail-closed tooling (markdownlint-cli2, codespell, lychee offline, awk shdoc comment-coverage) emitting foreman.docs-check.v1 JSON for gate consumption, rather than relying on reviewer vigilance; failures loop back to the implementer as a corrected spec.

nodes.label: bats-core test harness (tests/run.sh, setup_tmp_repo)
nodes.rationale: Each test creates a throwaway git repo under BATS_TEST_TMPDIR with an isolated FOREMAN_HOME so no test ever touches the real repo; added because shipped wt-* and gate scripts had grown with an empty tests/ directory.

nodes.label: Evidence contract (head SHA + status digests before/after)
nodes.rationale: Recording git HEAD and a SHA-256 digest of git status --porcelain before and after invoking the worker CLI makes unauthorized git activity mechanically detectable (unauthorized_git_activity flag) instead of trusting worker narration.
nodes.norm_label: evidence contract (head sha + status digests before/after)

nodes.label: Git-write ban (standing rule for workers)
nodes.rationale: Workers never run git write commands (commit/add/reset/branch/push/rebase/merge/tag) because the architect owns all git writes; keeping worker changes uncommitted keeps the blast radius reviewable before anything lands.

nodes.label: ARCHITECT_ACTIONS report field
nodes.rationale: Operations a lane cannot perform (deletions, renames, chmod under Grok's PermissionCancelled limit) are listed for the architect to execute instead of burning retries — four retries once cost ~17 minutes.

nodes.label: Vendored reference skills (scrapling, graphify, superpowers)
nodes.rationale: Vendoring full skill copies makes the Foreman install self-contained; staleness is accepted, VENDORED.md records provenance and the re-vendor procedure, and local-overlay files (*.local.md, cookie vaults) are stripped at vendor time.

nodes.label: Foreman Combined Skill Design (Fable Advisor + Original Foreman merge)
nodes.rationale: A single portable skill merges Fable Advisor soft orchestration (cost discipline, five-part specs, cross-vendor implementers, advisor) with the original Foreman hard harness (worktrees, external evidence, cold-diff audit, deterministic gate) rather than maintaining two skills.
nodes.norm_label: foreman combined skill design (fable advisor + original foreman merge)

nodes.label: First dogfood run lessons (five defects)
nodes.rationale: The site/ dogfood run surfaced: Grok lane drift with false narration and an unauthorized git commit; the headless PermissionCancelled wall; shared-checkout collisions from a concurrent session committing to main; an untested bash harness; and codex-auditor never exercised end-to-end. These five defects drive every enhancement goal.

nodes.label: Lane hardening (CS1: contracts, evidence, known limits)
nodes.rationale: Grok drifted from spec on four points while narrating success and ran unauthorized git commits; codified contracts (git-write ban, evidence digests, known-limits sections, ARCHITECT_ACTIONS) make drift detectable and impossible asks avoidable. CS1 lands first because later changesets' workers must obey it.
nodes.norm_label: lane hardening (cs1: contracts, evidence, known limits)

nodes.label: Worktree-by-default implement rounds
nodes.rationale: A concurrent session committed to main four times mid-run while implementers shared the main checkout; running every soft-mode implement round in its own worktree eliminates the collision class at the cost of one script call, even for trivial single-file edits.

nodes.label: Documentation & comment-quality stage (Section 5)
nodes.rationale: Toolset chosen after research: markdownlint-cli2 + codespell + lychee + shdoc convention + PSScriptAnalyzer; Vale prose linting was rejected for now because it has the highest setup cost and requires a maintained style package.

nodes.label: Cost discipline (prime directive)
nodes.rationale: The session model is the most expensive lane; the architect emits judgment (specs, routing, verdicts, short reports) instead of implementation volume, keeps context lean, and reasons once before handing off.

nodes.label: Five-part spec contract
nodes.rationale: Implementers share none of the architect's conversation context, so every delegation must be self-contained (Objective, Files, Interfaces, Constraints, Verification); a spec you cannot finish writing means the decision is not made.

nodes.label: Cross-vendor invariant (auditor vendor differs from worker vendor)
nodes.rationale: Same-family models share blind spots — the failure mode the skill buys insurance against; default pairing is Grok implements, Codex Sol audits; a lane never audits its own vendor's work and never silently substitutes the host model under another vendor's name.
nodes.norm_label: cross-vendor invariant (auditor vendor differs from worker vendor)

nodes.label: Hard-mode task loop (INIT to PR with deterministic gate)
nodes.rationale: All security-critical enforcement lives in bash scripts, not prompts; gate failure loops back to IMPLEMENT within max_rework_rounds and CI remains final authority.
nodes.norm_label: hard-mode task loop (init to pr with deterministic gate)

nodes.label: Audit verdict schema (APPROVED | WARNING | BLOCKED)
nodes.rationale: Auditor output is untrusted input to the architect/gate, not a final verdict to relay without reading the evidence.

nodes.norm_label: audit dimensions (acceptance, regressions, tampering, security, quality, prompt injection)

nodes.label: Known limits per CLI (soft mode, headless)
nodes.rationale: Grok headless cannot run shell commands (PermissionCancelled under acceptEdits) and may narrate success without writing; Codex workspace-write cannot write outside the workspace or install over network; both lanes lack conversation context — so specs must be self-contained and never ask Grok for deletions.
nodes.norm_label: known limits per cli (soft mode, headless)

nodes.label: Worktree lifecycle (wt-new, consolidate, cleanup)
nodes.rationale: Industry practice (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) treats git worktrees as the isolation primitive for multi-agent work: one object store, many checkouts, no file collisions; worktree creation is serialized via flock against a known git race, and reports land in ~/.foreman/runs/ for a durable audit trail independent of worktree lifetime.

nodes.label: Pre-implementation tool-check / bootstrap gate
nodes.rationale: Multi-step implementation must not start while must-tools fail inventory; bootstrap runs only after user confirmation and auth (grok login / codex login) is never automated.

nodes.label: Honest limits (containers share host/WSL2 kernel)
nodes.rationale: Containers share the host/WSL2 kernel, so Foreman claims defense-in-depth rather than absolute isolation; soft mode has residual risk (no automatic forbidden-path gate) and doctrine prefers failing closed when audit or checks infrastructure is missing.
